name: Chat Interceptor
description: Runs a per-room script before the agent replies; falls through to the AI when the script declines.

debug.description: Write a per-turn trace to logFile.

logFile.description: Absolute path of the debug trace file. Defaults to ~/.openclaw/logs/chat-interceptor.log

offstageLogFile.description: Absolute path of the file that records every message the AI never saw: turns a script handled, turns that ended in a script error, and /aside notes. One `<local time> <JSON>` line each; /tap reads it. Always on, regardless of debug. Defaults to ~/.openclaw/logs/chat-interceptor-offstage.log

fiat.description: Enables the /fiat command: start an AI coder (Claude Code through ccrun, or Codex through cdrun) on the project bound to the current room and have it run its /tap skill. A project is an OpenClaw skill (SKILL.md plus scripts/intercept.*); installing it copies it into the room's agent workspace with `openclaw skills install`, and the room's route runs the installed copy. Omit this block and /fiat only says it is not configured.

projectsDir.description: Directory holding one subdirectory per project. `/fiat <projname>` creates `<projectsDir>/<projname>/genesis/.tap` for a new project. A project's skill is the project folder itself when it has a SKILL.md, otherwise the one folder right under it that does.

projectsFile.description: Where the room-to-project table is kept, one entry per conversation: which project the room belongs to, whether its script is installed, and the open Claude Code session. Defaults to ~/.openclaw/chat-interceptor-projects.json. It holds conversation ids, so it lives in the state directory rather than in any project.

harness.description: Which AI /fiat starts when the command does not say -claude or -codex. Defaults to "claude".

ccrun.description: argv of ccrun (github.com/neritina-ai/cli-ccrun), which starts Claude Code in a console of its own with Remote Control on and types prompts into it by PID. Only needed for Claude Code. Defaults to ["ccrun"]. Use an absolute path: the gateway runs as a service and its PATH may differ from a shell.

cdrun.description: argv of cdrun (github.com/caridina-ai/cli-cdrun), which starts a background Codex session and sends prompts to it by PID. Only needed for Codex. Defaults to ["cdrun"]. Use an absolute path: the gateway runs as a service and its PATH may differ from a shell.

openclaw.description: argv of the openclaw CLI. /fiat uses it for two things: `message send` to post into the room, and `skills install <skill> --force --agent <id>` to install a project's skill into the room's agent. Defaults to ["openclaw"]. Use absolute paths, e.g. ["C:/Program Files/nodejs/node.exe", "<npm global root>/openclaw/openclaw.mjs"]: the gateway runs as a service and its PATH may differ from a shell.

interpreters.description: How to run a project script by file extension, as an argv prefix that the script path is appended to. Example: a .py entry of [C:/tools/uv.exe, run]. Only needed for extensions the plugin cannot resolve itself: .mjs/.js/.cjs always use the gateway's own Node binary, and .py falls back to uv (then python) found on PATH.

allowFrom.description: Sender ids allowed to run /fiat, on top of OpenClaw's own command authorization. Omit to allow every authorized sender. /fiat starts an agent that can write files on this machine.

routes.description: Per-conversation script routes. The first route whose channel and target match wins; no match means the turn goes to the AI unchanged.

name.description: Label used in traces and error messages.

channel.description: Channel/provider id, e.g. "telegram" or "discord". Omit to match any channel.

target.description: Conversation to intercept, in `openclaw message send --target` form. Bare ids ("-1001234567890"), prefixed ids ("channel:123456789012345678"), and fully qualified ids ("discord:channel:123456789012345678") all resolve to the same room.

project.description: Name of a directory under fiat.projectsDir. The script and the interpreter are worked out by convention every time the route runs: scripts/intercept.{mjs,js,cjs,py} inside that project, run with the gateway's own Node for JavaScript or with uv (then python) for Python. Nothing machine-specific ends up in the config, so it keeps working across Node and uv upgrades. Give this or command.

command.description: argv of the script, as an escape hatch when the project convention does not fit. Wins over project. Use absolute executable paths: the gateway runs as a service and its PATH may differ from a shell.

env.description: Extra environment variables merged over the gateway's own.

timeoutMs.description: Kill the script after this long. Defaults to 60000.

onError.description: What to do when the script fails. "handle" (default) replies with the error; "passthrough" hands the turn to the AI. Only use passthrough for scripts with no side effects.
